The loss stems from peso appreciation against the dollar—when the peso strengthens, reserve revaluations generate accounting losses for Banxico. Unlike 2024, when the peso depreciated and Banxico transferred 17.9 billion pesos, this year's appreciation provides no surplus for the treasury.

stories.summary: On May 1, Labor Day, President Sheinbaum signed the constitutional agreement formalizing the reduction of the standard work week from 48 hours to 40 hours. The reform, approved as a constitutional amendment, provides workers with an extra eight hours of rest per week while maintaining the same wage base. Sheinbaum framed it as a major achievement for working Mexicans and reaffirmed the government's commitment to labor rights.

The infrastructure project, constructed by SEDENA engineers, features three lanes for vehicles and a two-way bicycle path. The investment totaled 10.3 billion pesos and improves connectivity between Cancún's hotel zone and the city proper. The bridge is part of broader infrastructure modernization efforts.

stories.headline: Mexico City sinking at 10 inches per year due to groundwater depletion, NASA satellite data shows
stories.summary: According to new satellite imagery released by NASA, Mexico City is subsiding at a rate of nearly 10 inches (25 centimeters) per year, making it one of the world's fastest-sinking cities. The cause: extensive groundwater pumping for the city's water supply, combined with urban development, has dramatically shrunk the aquifer beneath the city. Built on a drained lake bed, many historic buildings and monuments are noticeably tilted from uneven sinking over more than a century of subsidence.

The first phase includes stations in Mérida, Cancún, and Palenque and establishes cargo transfer points. The project aims to integrate Mexico's major infrastructure projects and improve freight transport across the country.
